judicial_actions.holding_summary: Section 66A invalidated in entirety for being vague and overbroad, creating a chilling effect on speech.

judicial_actions.constitutional_ground: Articles 14, 19(1)(g), 21 read with CEDAW under Article 51(c)
judicial_actions.holding_summary: Supreme Court formulated binding guidelines to operate as law under Article 141 until statutory enactment.

judicial_actions.constitutional_ground: Article 44 / Secular application of Section 125 CrPC
judicial_actions.holding_summary: Section 125 CrPC applies universally to all divorced women irrespective of personal religion.
Struck down Section 497 IPC for violating dignity and autonomy of women, treating wife as chattel of husband.
Read down Section 377 IPC to exclude consensual sexual acts between consenting adults in private.

judicial_actions.statute_name: Code of Criminal Procedure 1973 (Arrest & Custodial Safeguards)
judicial_actions.holding_summary: Formulated 11 mandatory procedural guidelines for arrest and detention to prevent custodial violence.

legislative_responses.enacted_statute_or_amendment: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
legislative_responses.official_evidentiary_citation: Statement of Objects and Reasons, POSH Act 2013 (Bill No. 144 of 2010), citing Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan.
legislative_responses.detailed_evolution_notes: Parliament expressly cited the Vishaka guidelines and international commitments in the Statement of Objects and Reasons, codifying internal complaints committees and inquiries into comprehensive statute.

legislative_responses.enacted_statute_or_amendment: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986
legislative_responses.official_evidentiary_citation: Statement of Objects and Reasons, Muslim Women Act 1986, specifically addressing the aftermath of Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum.
legislative_responses.detailed_evolution_notes: Enacted to supersede the direct operation of Section 125 CrPC regarding Muslim divorced women, later harmoniously construed in Danial Latifi (2001).

legislative_responses.official_evidentiary_citation: Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs Report No. 246 (2023) on Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, affirming omission of adultery pursuant to Joseph Shine.
legislative_responses.detailed_evolution_notes: Adultery provision Section 497 was omitted completely from BNS 2023 in line with the Supreme Court constitutional bench decision in Joseph Shine.

legislative_responses.enacted_statute_or_amendment: Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Act, 2008 (Act 5 of 2009)
legislative_responses.official_evidentiary_citation: Law Commission of India 177th Report on Law Relating to Arrest (2001) and Statement of Objects & Reasons of CrPC Amendment Act 2008, citing D.K. Basu.
legislative_responses.detailed_evolution_notes: Insertion of Sections 41A, 41B, 41C, and 41D into CrPC directly codifying D.K. Basu arrest memo, notice of appearance, and right to meet advocate.
